newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman Aviation sees 1996 profits up 12 percent.
newsitem.headline: Oman Aviation sees 1996 profits up 12 percent.

text.p: Oman Aviation Services Company, which runs the small Gulf Arab state's international and domestic air services, expects profits of more than four million Omani rials ($10.6 million) in 1996, up 12 percent from 1995, the Omani News Agency said on Friday.
It quoted the company's general manager Awad bin Mohammad Bamukhalef as saying the profits were expected to rise 12 percent to more than four million rials from 3.6 million rials in 1995.
Oman Aviation Services, which is traded on the Muscat Securities Market, is 35 percent owned by Oman's government and the rest by Omani investors.
It runs Oman Air, which currently flies from Muscat to Bombay, Trivandrum, Colombo, Dhaka, Karachi, Kuwait and Dubai as well as operating domestic services. ($1=0.377 Omani rials)
